title: Google's Android Earthquake Alerts reached phones in Crete and the Dodecanese seconds before the 14 May 2025 M6.0 (Greek press 6.1) Kasos quake
summary: Android users in Crete and the Dodecanese got Google's quake alert seconds before the M6.0 (Greek press 6.1) Kasos quake of 14 May 2025.
account: At 01:51 local time on Wednesday 14 May 2025 (22:51 UTC on 13 May) a magnitude 6.0 (USGS; Greek outlets 6.1) earthquake struck 20 km south-south-east of Fry on Kasos, between Kasos and Karpathos, at 76 km depth; USGS logged 931 felt reports and a green alert level. Newsbomb, GizChina Greece, in.gr and Alphafreepress reported on 14 and 15 May that Google's Android Earthquake Alerts System, which in Europe detects quakes from phone accelerometers rather than seismographs, had notified users in Crete, the Dodecanese and farther away seconds before the shaking, by message and an audible signal similar to the 112 alert. None of the reports names a recipient, gives a lead time in seconds, or mentions damage or injuries.
purpose: Built to detect earthquakes from the accelerometers of Android phones, combine the signals on Google's servers and push an alert to users in the expected shaking zone ahead of the slower seismic waves, for quakes of magnitude 4.5 and above; this alert was that intended function.
system: Android Earthquake Alerts System (crowdsourced phone-accelerometer detection; alerts for magnitude 4.5 and above)
domain: Disaster risk reduction / earthquake early warning
taxonomy_note: No category names early warning or harm prevention; Accessibility is the closest because the documented effect is that residents received a timely alert, matching the Alanya 2022 Android-alert record. Protective response with prevention unproven: four Greek outlets say the alert arrived seconds before the shaking, but no recipient, lead time, protective action or averted injury is documented, and the quake caused no reported harm.

ratings.reason: An unstated number of Android users in Crete, the Dodecanese and farther away received a few seconds' message and audible notice of a deep M6.0 quake; the fetched reports name no recipient, give no lead time in seconds and report no damage, injuries or protective action.

ai_role.statement: If the reports are right, the alert was produced end to end by Google's system: accelerometer triggers from many phones combined on Google's servers to detect the quake, then alerts pushed ahead of the slower waves, as Google's 2020 description and the 2025 Science paper set out. Google's own pages do not use the words AI or machine learning; the Science abstract speaks of smartphone-based earthquake detection algorithms, and the OECD Monitor classifies the system as AI doing event detection. That alerts arrived seconds before shaking rests on unattributed statements in four Greek outlets published within a day of the quake; none quotes a recipient, a seismologist or Google, and no Google per-event confirmation was found.

produced_by: A magnitude 6.0 (USGS) quake above the system's 4.5 alert threshold, centered offshore south of Kasos at about 76 km depth, so a push alert could outrun the slower waves to Crete and the Dodecanese

Enough Android phones near the epicentre with the Earthquake Alerts setting on to trigger Google's server-side detection; in Europe the system uses the accelerometers in phones instead of seismographs (in.gr)
Receiving phones with location (GPS) enabled and an internet connection, which Alphafreepress lists as requirements for the alerts
must_hold: The server's magnitude and location estimate must be right and early: the 2025 Science paper reports that only 36% of alert recipients got the alert before shaking
Recipients must know what to do with seconds of notice; the Greek reports document no protective action by anyone who received the alert
The phone must have the Earthquake Alerts setting enabled (Alphafreepress: Settings > Safety & Emergency > Earthquake Alerts) and the feature must be supported in the region

headline: Google alerts Crete phones seconds before the M6.0 Kasos quake

revisions.change: Record drafted from the OECD Monitor entry and the cited sources. Dated to 14 May 2025 local time: USGS gives the origin as 2025-05-13T22:51:15 UTC, M6.0 mww, 76 km depth, 20 km SSE of Fry, and in.gr places it in the early hours of Wednesday; Newsbomb's text says the early hours of Tuesday 13 May, which contradicts both and is not followed. Greek outlets report 6.1; USGS 6.0. Filed as protective response with prevention unproven as the classifier proposed. Of the Monitor's eight Greek sources, Newsbomb, GizChina Greece, in.gr and Alphafreepress state that users were alerted before the shaking (Newsbomb names Crete, the Dodecanese and farther away, by message and an audible signal like the 112 alert); Parapolitika is an explainer without that claim; eleftherostypos.gr and reader.gr returned HTTP 403 and ant1news.gr a TLS error, so they were not read. No Google statement about this event was found; web search was unavailable in this session, so sourcing is limited to the Monitor's list, USGS, Google's own pages and the Science abstract.

claim_basis: Four independent news reports, one independent dataset, the makers' peer-reviewed study and two press releases from the makers are on file. There is no independent study or report and no finding by a regulator or court.
